_doc: Independent reference oracle, money kind. Asserts that LifetimeGiftExemptions leaves the chargeable value of one lifetime gift after the exemptions gov.uk lists and IHTA 1984 enacts: small gifts (s.20), gifts in consideration of marriage or civil partnership (s.22), and the £3,000 annual exemption with one year's carry-forward (s.19). The allowance already used this year and the carry-forward still available are inputs: s.19(3) and (3A) decide which transfer in a year takes the exemption first, and that ordering is the caller's. Normal expenditure out of income (s.21) needs a judgement about the donor's income and standard of living, so the rule routes it to a person; that leg is asserted in the rule's own fixtures because this harness asserts only computed figures. Figures read from gov.uk and legislation.gov.uk on sourced_at.
statute: IHTA 1984 s.19 (annual exemption), s.20 (small gifts), s.22 (gifts in consideration of marriage or civil partnership)

cases.label: mark-2000-to-jane
cases.citation_quote: In the 2023 to 2024 tax year, Mark gave £2,000 to his daughter Jane. If he died within 7 years of the gift, this would use £2,000 of his annual exemption.
cases.note: Covered by the year's £3,000 (s.19(1)); £1,000 is left to carry forward (s.19(2)).

cases.label: mark-4000-to-sarah-with-carry-forward
cases.citation_quote: In the following 2024 to 2025 tax year, Mark gave £4,000 to his other daughter Sarah. If Mark died within 7 years of the gift, this would use his annual exemption of £3,000 plus the £1,000 of annual exemption left over from the previous tax year.
cases.note: £3,000 of the year (s.19(1)) then the £1,000 carried (s.19(2)).

cases.label: mark-5000-exceeds-both-years
cases.citation_quote: Transfers of value made by a transferor in any one year are exempt to the extent that the values transferred by them (calculated as values on which no tax is chargeable) do not exceed £3,000. ... Where those values fall short of £3,000, the amount by which they fall short shall, in relation to the next following year, be added to the £3,000
cases.note: Derived from the statute: £5,000 less £3,000 less the £1,000 carried = £1,000 chargeable.

cases.label: wedding-child-5000-plus-annual-3000
cases.citation_quote: For example, you can give your child a wedding gift of £5,000 as well as £3,000 using your annual exemption in the same tax year.
cases.note: s.22(1)(a) £5,000 by a parent of a party, then s.19(1) £3,000.

cases.label: wedding-grandchild-10000
cases.citation_quote: in the case of gifts within subsection (2) below by a parent of a party to the marriage or civil partnership ... £5,000, ... in the case of other gifts within subsection (2) below, £2,500, and ... in any other case £1,000
cases.note: Derived from the statute: a grandparent's outright gift to a grandchild is within s.22(2)(a) but not by a parent, so £2,500 (s.22(1)(b)); then £3,000 annual (s.19(1)); £10,000 − £2,500 − £3,000 = £4,500.

cases.label: small-gift-250
cases.citation_quote: Transfers of value made by a transferor in any one year by outright gifts to any one person are exempt if the values transferred by them (calculated as values on which no tax is chargeable) do not exceed £250.
cases.note: Exempt under s.20; the annual exemption is not used.
